title: Cling to God alone; love with whole soul; after courage, foundations
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK SIX. That we must cling to God alone who is God by nature, and love him from whole soul and heart.

Cyril: Concerning the manliness understood in Christ, then, and spiritual good-strength, a sufficient word has been worked out by us, as it seems, Palladius; yet the things upon which these would come to be from our side it is necessary to look around at, as I think, again.
Palladius: You speak well.
Cyril: Come then already, turning the eye of the mind round in a circle, and going unto exact examination

title: Faith the foundation; first commandment; jealous God
english: of the things that concern us, let us look well which path going along we shall be bright, and shall bind on ourselves as it were some crown the vote upon all the things praised. Or do I not seem to you to think rightly, having chosen to be curious in these things at least?

Palladius: Altogether so. For I myself also would say that one must be whetted beforehand by the challenge toward manliness, and choose the things through which someone would be bright, and would come straight toward the blameless life.

Cyril: Therefore let us already say that of every house the support is a foundation; and of a temple the keel is a beginning; and of the one who has chosen to set things right, a foundation and beginning of a base would be the knowledge of the truth, and the unadulterated word concerning faith into the one God who is by nature and true: ‘For if you do not believe, you will not even understand,’ says the sacred Letter. And those understanding must not yet be idle of the necessary things, not knowing how to set right. Or would you not say it is necessary toward our being well-approved, the examination upon every thing to be done, if we have made in word the doing rightly what it is necessary to love?
Palladius: I say so.

Cyril: Faith therefore is nurse of understanding. And understanding makes the testing of the things to be done for us. And indeed when the God of all set over those from Israel as it were some pedagogue and wise director—the law through Moses—he laid down beforehand as it were some base and unshaken beginning the knowledge from the one and true Godhead; for he supposed they would not be strong enough to reach the blameless and pure life, or to be rhythm-trained by the introducer of the finest things—the law—and to yield to commandments, unless having taken the faith upon God into mind as a fore-wall they should nobly stand against the pleasures that whet them unto slackness. It was necessary then, necessary, that those of old lay aside beforehand as it were some soul-sickness the polytheist wandering, and be well fixed by the faith into the one God by nature and truly; therefore also first a law shone forth to them: ‘I am the Lord your God, who led you out from Egypt’s land from a house of slavery. There will not be for you other gods besides me. You will not make for yourself an idol, nor likeness of anything as many as are in the heaven above, and in the earth below, and as many as are in the waters under the earth; you will not worship them, nor will you serve them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, paying back fathers’ sins upon children unto a third and fourth generation to those who hate me; and doing mercy unto thousands to those who love me and keep my ordinances.’ For it was necessary, necessary, that those about to make the commandment unmovable be terrified with hard fears; therefore he also names himself a jealous God, and one who lays fathers’ sins upon those from them, if indeed they should choose to live according to those ones, and

title: Fathers’ sins; vain Name; idols; Trinity without polytheism
english: to race with ancestral stumblings. For we do not say somewhere that fathers’ sins strike down upon those who have altogether done nothing wrong, although God has cried out expressly: ‘Fathers will not die on behalf of children, nor children on behalf of fathers; each will die in his own sin.’ Yet if those from them should follow the fathers’ judgments, and be zealots of ancestral impiety, the wrath somehow stretches even unto them. And even if somehow from inborn love-of-humanity the God above all should let go the first ones from needing to be punished, yet late he brings upon the second or the third the anger fitting and owed at the beginnings to the profane race. He was therefore frightening them unto needing to fear, naming himself a jealous God; yet he was also confirming them otherwise unto faith, promising to do mercy unto thousands to those who love him. And he was adding to these a neighboring and sister commandment: ‘For you will not take,’ he says, ‘the name of the Lord your God upon a vain thing; for the Lord will not cleanse the one taking his name upon a vain thing.’ Some were doing this, fastening the calling of God upon woods and stones, and unlearnedly bringing down the name above every name unto a handiwork and toil of a human hand. And God said somewhere concerning them through Isaiah’s voice: ‘A craftsman choosing a wood stood it in a measure, and in glue shaped it, and made it as a form of a man, and as beauty of a human to stand it in a house; he cut wood from the thicket which the Lord planted, and rain lengthened it, that it might be for humans unto burning, and taking from it he was warmed, and having burned they baked breads upon them; yet the remainder they worked into gods, and they worship them.’ And after other things: ‘Know that their heart is ash, and they wander.’ These take the Lord’s name upon a vain thing. Yet I think those who have already come to be outside a diabolic snare, and have known the true God, must not kneel unto cold thoughts, nor honor the ignoble in this at least with empty talk, being dragged opposite unto needing to know other gods, or to think that any exist at all beside the one and truly. ‘For even if some are called gods and lords, both in heaven and upon earth, yet for us one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we unto him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him; and one Holy Spirit, in whom are all things, and we in him.’ For we least of all contract the nature of the Godhead in a Jewish way unto only the one God and Father, yet widening as it were unto a holy and consubstantial Trinity; and indeed also distinguishing by quality of persons and property of hypostasis, we contract again unto one God, because of the sameness of substance, and we will serve him, we will worship him, calling upon the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. ‘For there will not be,’ he says, ‘other gods besides me;’ and again: ‘The Lord your God you will wor

title: One God; no limping both ways; no second baptism after apostasy
english: ship, and him alone you will serve.’ And since there is one God the Father, and one Lord the Son, and one Holy Spirit proceeding, we will neither carry out the one God from true lordship; nor indeed will we send out the one who is truly and by nature Lord from being God; for lordship will altogether follow the Godhead according to nature; and again to lordship according to truth, the glory of the Godhead.
Palladius: Most rightly and most wisely you have spoken.

Cyril: One God therefore, Palladius, we will know, and upon him we will count no one at all, making the unholy and profane double-souledness, as boastful and truly insolent, farthest from our own soul, in order that a sacred word may not also cry out upon us ourselves: ‘How long will you limp upon both hams? either Baal Baal, or God God.’ For we must be seen single-turned, not other-minded and shaken, falling most ready into what is not fitting; as for limping upon both and loving to be tossed, I would say it is of the most godless things. And indeed the ancient law also honors with death the one not secure, for it says: ‘The one sacrificing to gods will be wiped out, except to the Lord alone.’ Therefore to lift oneself against the divine glory, and to distribute the things fitting it and it alone to whomever someone might choose, and to favor with them those not gods by nature, would be a most shameful of sicknesses, or rather an accusation and indictment of the last impiety. It is necessary therefore to have been freed from such things, the one at least who is truly genuine and God-loving, and not only cleansing the heart, but not even so much as to say ever sending through the tongue the idol name. For it has been written that ‘And you will not remember a name of other gods, nor will it be heard from your mouth.’ For what it is shameful to know, it is not without penalty to speak. And having chosen to honor the genuine in faith everywhere, it is fitting to remember blessed Paul writing thus: ‘For it is impossible that those once enlightened, and having tasted a good utterance of God, and powers of a coming age, and having fallen aside, be renewed again unto repentance.’ For those once brought unto partaking of the heavenly and divine grace through the holy baptism, and having received the true and life-giving word concerning resurrection and Christ’s kingdom, if they should choose to run back toward what was at the beginnings, and to run under the first sickness, they will not be renewed toward cleansing through a second baptism; ‘For their unbelief will not abolish God’s faith,’ as divine Paul says. Nor because some have despised going backward the divine grace will we write down the insecure; yet rather the Judge of all will subject to penalties those not declining to slide down unto this impiety, as having trampled the Son of God and counted the blood of the covenant common, and having insulted the Spirit of grace, in whom

title: Destroy idols after Jordan; bless bread/wine/water as mysteries
english: they were sanctified, and have become sharers of the divine nature. For just as a soldier who has thrown away the shield and fled the war must not be honored with second sealings, but already be punished, and pay accounts of unmanliness; in the same manner, I think, those so insulting a reverend and admirable grace must not be honored with a second gift of the Spirit, the first having been set aside, but already it is fitting they lie under penalties. For that those once enlightened must come unto this judgment and steadiness of reasonings—to know one God by nature, and to abominate those introducing something other beside this, and to make finest of desires the leaping upon idols, and shaking down temples, and counting the Greeks’ worships nothing—an ancient word will also teach us. For it has been written in Numbers: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses on the west of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, and you will say toward them: You are crossing the Jordan into Canaan’s land, and you will destroy all who dwell in the land before your face. And you will lift out their lookouts, and all their cast idols you will destroy them, and all their steles you will lift out.’ You understand that those who have passed the Jordan must make altars and precincts from the midst, and pry up without care the idols themselves and steles? as for allotting sparing perhaps to such evils, it would become a clear indication of not having been fixed well, nor dedicating the heart unaccused to God, although he says clearly concerning the godless and evil: ‘You will not worship their gods, nor will you serve according to their works, but with a taking-down you will take down, and crushing you will crush their steles, and you will serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water; and I will turn weakness away from you; there will not be barren, nor sterile upon your land; I will fill up the number of your days.’ For it is not unclear that for those very well fixed and from a healthy mind clinging to the God of all, and having practiced to make a clear demonstration of the matter—the shaking down of altars and steles, and playthings of humans corrupted in mind—it will be a procurer of divine gifts.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: For if indeed you should take down the hand-made things, he says, and should serve God, having hated the customs beside those ones, ‘I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water.’ The word is mystical and deep; for for those genuine toward God, the partaking of Christ’s mysteries will be unto spiritual blessing, and the grace through the holy baptism. Yet for those still double-souled, moved unto apostasy, wrath and condemnation; and what of the terrible things is the sharing of the spiritual blessing not? and this,

title: Worthy Eucharist; smash high places; do not copy nations’ rites
english: I think, is what wise Paul also said, that ‘The one eating and drinking the body and blood of Christ unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. Yet let a human test himself,’ he says, ‘and then eat from the bread, and drink from the cup;’ The partaking of the holy mysteries will therefore be unto blessing, he says, for those at least who are truly most God-loving. And they will be freed from softening—that is, from being ready to be sick with what is by nature unjust, and carrying off unto unmanliness; yet neither will there be barren among them, he says, nor sterile. For every God-loving and holy soul is most fertile, and leafy with holy fruits—I mean again the boasts from virtue.
Palladius: So it is.

Cyril: And not allowing to have the heart easy to shake, he skillfully turns us toward needing to choose what stands firm unto faith, and securely unto piety; for sometimes educating by fitting reasonings unto the better, he commands to be eager away from—or rather to turn away altogether, as procurer of ruin—the sacrificing to idols or worshiping, showing such a sickness full of the last slander, or rather of the highest impiety; and sometimes also setting fear—I mean that of being punished—as it were some pedagogue and noble guard for us, he turns us from every side unto what pleases him. And indeed in Deuteronomy blessed Moses says: ‘And these are the ordinances and the judgments which you will keep to do upon the land which the Lord the God of your fathers gives you in a lot all the days which you live upon the earth. With destruction you will destroy all the places in which the nations served their gods there, whom you inherit, upon the high mountains, and upon the dunes, and under a leafy tree. And you will dig down their altars, and smash their steles, and cut out their groves, and the carved things of their gods you will burn with fire, and you will destroy their name from that place.’ The wise and select of Greeks, and poets especially, name some mountain-nymphs and tree-nymphs, or demons. And there are those who having chosen to honor the gods beside themselves with the heights according to place, setting altars on mountains, were eager to sacrifice oxen, and having settled around the more well-grown of the trees groves and images of demons, were using sheep-slaughters. Yet it was necessary that those come to be under God who is according to truth and by nature, dreading nothing, shake down the playthings of the wanderers, and go as far as possible from the customs beside those ones. Therefore he says again: ‘And if the Lord your God should wipe out the nations unto whom you go there to inherit their land, from your face, and you should inherit them, and settle in their land, take heed to yourself, lest you seek to follow along with them after they have been wiped out from your face; you will not seek their gods, saying, How do these nations do to their

title: No child-sacrifice; false prophet dies; God tests love
english: gods, I will also do; you will not do thus to the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did to their gods, because they also burn their sons and their daughters in fire to their gods.’ Well does the lawgiver forbid altogether the imitation of the wanderers, and very well commands to stand off from the merciless slaughter of children. And he convicts as destroyers and ruiners of humanity the blood-loving and falsely-named gods, who even savagely dishonor the laws of necessary affection, for the sake of what seems good to them; ‘For God created the all unto being, and the generations of the world are saving, and there is not a kingdom of Hades upon earth. Yet by envy of a devil death entered into the world.’ And the divine will overturns death, and dissolves corruption; and hates that the things that are should not be; for he created the all unto being, according as it has been written. Yet those netted unto wandering by the demons’ greediness bring forward to Satan as it were seasonings, and of the most useful and sweet-smelling incense, the destruction of those come to be unto life, and the death of those created unto being. Most skillfully therefore he wished to show that the customs beside those ones are full of the last slander, and nature being wronged, and the ordinances of much-prayed-for love-of-children being trampled, very well hustling the noble and evil-hating mind of the hearers unto needing to honor and choose swiftly whatever he himself would wish and say. And these things were legislated of old unto overturning of the unholiness beside those ones. Yet he also defines death for the one wishing to persuade away the one who has been fixed, and who has received in a God-loving way the knowledge of the truth. For he said thus again: ‘And if a prophet should rise among you or a dreamer of a dream, and should give you a sign or wonder, and the sign or the wonder should come which he spoke toward you, saying: Let us go and serve other gods whom you have not known, you will not hear the words of that prophet or of that dreamer of that dream, because the Lord your God is testing you to know whether you love your God from your whole heart, and from your whole soul; behind the Lord your God you will go, and him you will fear, and his commandments you will keep, and his voice you will hear, and him you will serve, and to him you will be added. And that prophet or that dreamer of the dream will die; for he spoke to make you wander away from the Lord your God.’ How holy and fitting to God the law! For if indeed for murderers of bodies death must follow altogether and in every way according to laws, how would the one bringing the ruinous wandering upon a soul, and casting the better than body into pits of destruction, according to the Savior’s own voice, not reasonably be in danger? That the deceiver and buffoon must have the justice upon blood done, God judged right;

title: Death for apostasy; love God above kin; broken cisterns
english: and he votes the equal penalty also upon the easily-carried and light mind of those subjected to such things. For when it was possible easily to flee, he says, waking up toward the true, for what did he make the voluntary running-off unto what wrongs? ‘And if there should be found among you in one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you, a man or woman who will do the evil opposite the Lord your God, to pass by his covenant, and going away they should serve other gods, and worship them—the sun or the moon, or any of those from the cosmos of the heaven, which he did not command you—and it was not announced to you, and you will seek very much, and behold the word has become true, this abomination has come to be in Israel; and you will lead out that human, or that woman, who did this evil deed, and you will stone them with stones, and they will die; upon two witnesses or upon three witnesses the one dying will die; he will not die upon one witness; and the hand of the witnesses will be upon him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people at the last; and you will lift out the evil from yourselves;’ For when God has been wronged concerning his own worship, to pity is not secure. And altogether harmful is not to be soft at the right time toward unmanly mutual-affections; and this, I think, is what the Lord said: ‘The one loving father or mother above me is not worthy of me.’ For let even then a law of affection go away, and let a power of natural love depart, and every thing whatever of the things coming unto love-of-humanity, and that we may speak thus, let God be served through a pious hardness. Or do you not say it is holy that those having unexcused the apostasy must be punished without pity, as grieving the glory beyond all, and not declining to insult without guard him whom it was somehow better to gladden with eagernesses unto steadfastness?
Palladius: Holy—for how not?

Cyril: And I will remember him saying through to those more ancient: ‘What wrong did your fathers find in me, that they stood away from me far, and went behind the vain things, and were made vain?’ And as it were astonished at the undiluted unlearnings of those from Israel, he says somehow thus: ‘Heaven was astonished upon this, and the earth shuddered still more very much, says the Lord; because my people did two evil things. Me they left—a spring of living water—and they dug for themselves crushed cisterns, which will not be able to hold water.’ For I would think, and very reasonably, that those standing off from the worship unto God, serving the creation beside the Creator and Maker, or still leaping down toward a more shameful wandering, worshiping the works of their own hands, miss every good-counsel; although it was easy, if indeed they should choose to think rightly, to look down upon the beauty of the nature above all and unspeakable from the creation of a world, and from the good-order of the things come to be to understand the orderer and leader and craftsman of this all. Yet having spat upon the so reverend and admirable judgment, some of the

title: Wood ‘father’; fake piety; God near sees all
english: more ancient exchanged golden things for bronze, according to the poets beside Greeks. For having let go the needing to worship God who is according to nature, they turned childishly toward useless random-worship; pouring shame and laughter upon their own head, and having chosen a self-called falling-away from the help from above. And indeed God said: ‘As a thief’s shame when he is caught, so will the sons of Israel themselves be shamed, and their kings, and their rulers, and their priests, and their prophets; to the wood they said, You are my father, and to the stone: You begot me. And they turned backs upon me, and not their faces; and in the time of their evils they will say: Rise and save us. And where are your gods, whom you made for yourself? If they will rise and save you in the time of your ill-treatment? because according to the number of your cities were your gods, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s ways they were sacrificing to Baal. Why do you speak toward me? All you have lawlessly acted unto me, says the Lord.’
Palladius: Terrible truly is the matter, friend.

Cyril: Yet someone sometimes of those finishing among us, not yet very much fixed, yet having practiced a plastered and bastard love unto Christ, and such as putting around himself as it were a fleece the seeming to be God-loving, will be a bitter and unholy beast, both a monkey and facing-both-ways, so as at home and by night—I mean the having-escaped-notice—to cling to the demons’ worships, and somehow to think reasonably that he himself also can run past God, and out-reason the mind of the unspeakable nature. And one would show even very without-toil that the one for whom these things are present to think has chosen the more shameful things of the Greeks’ silliness. For to the wise beside Greeks it seemed to hold rightly that the sun, being created and begotten—the great light-bearer, and made upon this very thing from beside God—sees all and hears all; for they thought that what has been taken along in a God’s rank must be rich with the dignities of the divine nature. And a dignity of the highest nature is to know and look down upon the all. Yet those ones in these things; and to us God was calling of old: ‘I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far; will anything be hidden from me?’ For nothing would escape the one who is truly God by nature. And let blessed David mystagogue saying: ‘Understand already, senseless ones among the people, and fools, sometime be thoughtful; the one who planted the ear, will he not hear? and the one who shaped eyes, will he not understand?’ Some were saying, I think, from ununderstanding: ‘The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand.’ Or is it not altogether silly to say that the supplier of knowledge neither knows, nor to think that the one giving the matter to those come to be from beside him does not hear?

title: Worship God alone; no omens; hear the prophet like Moses—Christ
english: Palladius: Altogether unpersuasive.

Cyril: One must therefore worship the Lord God alone and whole-turned, according to the Scriptures, and no one other beside him. For it has been written that ‘You will be perfect opposite the Lord your God.’ And spiritual perfectness is the being settled in faith, and blameless unto worship, and the unaccused beauty of the love unto God.
Palladius: So I say.

Cyril: Therefore, Palladius, those who have least chosen to worship other gods, or the creation beside the one who created—yet somehow being persuaded by the false-prophecies of the idol-servers—will we free from blame and accusation? or safely show free of the charges unto apostasy to those at least who are truly genuine?
Palladius: Not at all.

Cyril: And star-sorceries and omen-takings and false-prophecies, and demonic trickings, would fit, I think somewhere, only and perhaps those who have most outlandishly been eager to settle into mind the inglorious and cursed idolatry.

Palladius: You have spoken rightly. Since indeed a divine word also charges us that we must abominate the shamefulness unto these at least. And it holds thus: ‘And if you should enter into the land which the Lord your God gives you, you will not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations; there will not be found in you one purifying his son and his daughter in fire, one prophesying a prophecy, and taking omens, and observing birds, a sorcerer, singing a charm, a ventriloquist, and wonder-watcher, and asking the dead; for every one doing these is an abomination to the Lord your God.’ And after other things again he says: ‘You will be perfect before the Lord your God; these nations, whom you will inherit them, these will hear omen-takings and prophecies; yet not thus has the Lord your God given to you. A prophet from your brothers like me the Lord your God will raise; [him you will hear according to all as many as you asked from beside the Lord your God] at Horeb on the day of the assembly.’

Cyril: Well done, friend. For we will follow not wonder-watchers and dead-diviners, nor will we receive flights of birds as some true matter, even if they should be borne toward the right, or then unto the left; even if toward evening and toward dawn; for these things are of the last folly. Yet making Christ the prophet for us and among us the leader of the all, from him we will take the knowledge of the necessary things, and we will sit beside him, saying a long wail to the demons’ false-speakings and ‘farewell.’ For to God alone as it were will the needing to make-alive and to rule the all be laid down naturally and specially;

title: Foreknowledge God’s alone; demons are liars; do not credit oracles
english: in the same manner, I think, also the having knowledge of all things. And proper to his nature is clearly to know the things about to be, and to have as it were gathered in himself the form of the all. Or is the word upon this not both wise and exact?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: Toward him then we will sin, and toward the highest glory the writing will, if we believe that in profane and unclean spirits there are the things through which he himself would be beautified and is exceedingly splendid. It is already time for those disposed thus to suppose emptily also that Satan can make-alive, and even is a craftsman, if we will gift to him the most exceptional things of all and those specially laid down for God’s nature, and say they have grown upon him; and a proper and exceptional good of the highest nature is the knowledge of the things about to be. Or is what I say not true?

Palladius: Very much. For he says through Isaiah’s voice toward some assigning to the creation the things of God: ‘Remember these things, and groan; repent, you who have wandered, turn in the heart, and remember former things from the age, that I am God, and there is not still besides me one announcing beforehand the last things before they come to be, and at once it was finished, and I said: All my counsel will stand, and all as many as I have counseled I will do.’ For he was setting for the hearers as it were an indication of there not being any other by nature and truly God beside him—the being able to announce the last things before they come to be.

Cyril: Well done, Palladius. And I would still wish us looking around well at the true also to examine this: in what manner still, if we finish at all among those wishing to live rightly and evangelically, will we follow the flatteries of false-prophecies and indeed also, having attended as if some word from beside them were true, not mark off the Savior’s voice as needing to be false? For he said somewhere also toward the boastful and insolent Jews: ‘You are from your father the devil, and you wish to do your father’s desires; that one was a human-killer from a beginning, and in the truth he has not stood, because there is not truth in him; whenever he speaks the lie, he speaks from his own things, because he is a liar, and the father of it.’ In what manner then will a liar be unerring? and how not altogether and in every way misspeaking, the one not having stood in the truth? Is it then clear, Palladius, already somehow to everyone, that assigning the true to the demons’ voices we will vote against Christ the false-myth, and will say that the truth speaks falsely?
Palladius: We are in danger.
Cyril: And otherwise—for I would add also this to what has been said—we have been taught from beside Christ not to receive the words of the unclean spirits, even if

title: Christ silences true-speaking demons; Leviticus against mediums
english: they should sometime wish to bring forward the truth untrodden by them and most unaccustomed.
Palladius: And how do you say?

Cyril: Or do you not hear the holy evangelists having written that the demons, crying out something piercing and great, were coming toward Christ: ‘Ah, what to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene? You have come to destroy us; we know who you are, the Holy One of God. Yet he rebuking,’ it says, ‘was not allowing them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.’ And yet why ever—for according to likelihood someone might hesitate—did Christ rebuke those crying out the true? Yet the thing done was somehow beneficial unto us. For that one must not cling to the words from beside those ones, even if they should wish to cry out the truth itself, and to say the things clearly genuine, we are taught through this; for weaving sometimes the lie with the truth, they harm the hearers, not in another manner, I think, than as one might watch those who by mixture of honey take away the perception of bitter things, and by intertwining of sweet things wish to steal what sometimes grieves.
Palladius: Altogether slippery then is attending to the oracle-speakers’ trickings.

Cyril: God honors the matter with death, and writes it among the last evils. And he said thus in Leviticus: ‘And a soul which should follow after ventriloquists or enchanters, so as to whore after them, I will set my face upon that soul, and I will destroy it from its people; and you will be holy, because I am holy—Lord your God.’ And after other things again: ‘And a man or woman who should become among them a ventriloquist or enchanter, with death let them be put to death, and with stones stone them; they are liable.’ For first he refuses that any must love to follow the buffoon star-prophecies, or then necromancies, saying the matter is as far as possible from holy-fitting citizenship, and altogether unfitting for those clinging to God; and he defines death of the second, and says even they themselves are liable; not allowing pity to be allotted from our side to those who have already been driven unto this baseness, as to become a snare of death, and a hunt of guiltless souls, and a door of ruin, and a trapdoor of Hades, and what not of such evils? Yet I think somehow it is wise and unalloyed to understand that God would not have fixed so bitter a justice running beyond every evil upon those able to know and speak to others the things about to be, if indeed they truly had to speak of the things about to be. For a myth of the truth is not punished, yet the speaking-falsely is accursed; yet if someone should be caught doing this, and this as from God, he has somehow slandered the unspeakable nature itself, and assigning the lie to the truth as fitting it, having endured a justice equal to the charges he will go away unto that very much. Cyril: Very much; for a divine law will also straightway persuade us unto this. For God said thus in Deuteronomy: ‘And if someone should say in a heart: How will we know the word which the Lord has not spoken? as many as that prophet should speak upon the Lord’s name, and the word should not come to be which the Lord has not spoken, in impiety the prophet has spoken; you will not hold off from him.’ You hear that he says the failures in the things foretold will be a clear demonstration of something not having been oracled from God? for the truth loves truth. Some such thing he says through Jeremiah’s voice: ‘I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far; if a human will be hidden in hidden places, will I not also see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord. Have I heard what the prophets speak—false things which the prophets prophesy in my name?’ Then through the middle having accused not a little those who have despised the divine laws, he gives the truth as a clear demonstration of both the things from God and not. For he said again: ‘The prophet in whom is his dream, and in whom is my word toward him, let him narrate my word upon truth.’ As if something should appear having missed the truth, it would show at once its begetter false-speaking, and speaking from his own heart, not from the Lord’s mouth, according as it has been written.
Palladius: Do you wish we should set something of the necessary things unto a test, or leaving it go wherever your word should carry us?

Cyril: And indeed, Palladius, of the necessary things unto benefit our word is not short; as for not saying the seeming freely I would accuse, and very reasonably; speak then having hesitated at nothing.

Palladius: If some do not speak from the Lord’s mouth, yet belch, as you say, the things from a heart, in what manner then did that ventriloquist woman bring forward holy Samuel already dead to Saul, clarifying for him the end of the things about to be for him? for some think these things have been done thus, and not otherwise.

Cyril: And do you yourself think it does not hold thus, and will you reckon this better, or then do you say emptily that the righteous one’s soul was truly forced out, and came when a little woman was calling?

title: Necromancy not of God; saints’ souls not demons’ playthings
english: Palladius: I would not have to say clearly. Yet the test, I think somewhere, would show the true.

Cyril: You have spoken well. Therefore let that be busied with before the others for now—whether these things are busied with and wondered and finished through God, or then through evil spirits for whom the practice is a care.

Palladius: And who would come unto this absurdity of reasonings, so as to think that necromancers and ventriloquists and enchanters wonder these things through God? For I will remember the law determining the last penalty for everyone who has chosen to do this. Then how is it not stricken to understand that the one condemned with death is not out of tune with God? for he will not yet fight against his own laws.

Cyril: You think most excellently. And will we think the saints’ souls freed from bodies have been thrown aside, and are counted worthy of no word, and have already come unto this misery, so as even to lie under evil and unclean spirits, and unwillingly to follow those turning them easily wherever they should happen to choose? And yet wise John composing for us the book of the Apocalypse, which has also been honored with the Fathers’ votes, was affirming clearly that he had seen the saints’ souls under the divine altar itself. And if they even drag them from the upper dwellings themselves, and bring them down unsparingly from the most holy places, nothing hindering, heaven is walkable for all the demons, and paradise’s gate is opened for them according to likelihood; and the flaming sword also yields, as it seems, and not only of entrance and exit for them; but if they should wish also to bring out some of those come inside from free-speech; then is this not to tear down the hope in Christ, and to show thrice-wretched the life of those admired?
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And indeed it is not unclear. And how was it better for admirable Paul, to depart, and to be with Christ? For if indeed we are about, having gone away from earthly things, and having come to be with Christ, to lie under the opposing spirits, the faith has been emptied, according to what has been written, and everyone, I think, will then vote that being at home in a body differs incomparably from being with Christ, and what is more unbearable upon this; for still making our pastimes in this life, we have not been yoked under the devil’s wills, yet we tread rather upon snakes and scorpions, and upon all the enemy’s power, according to the Savior’s voice. Then having come to be with Christ, how will we be in worse things? and how does he himself speak truly saying: ‘My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me, and I give them eternal life, and they will not perish unto the age, and no one will snatch them from my hands; the Father

These things then are nonsense, and a terrible stroke, to think according to truth that a prophet’s voice was dragged down by cold charms of a most foul little woman from the places allotted to her.

Cyril: Setting beside the sacred Letter itself, we will then make clear the things coming unto mind, holding everywhere tightly of what is fitting. And it holds thus: ‘And Samuel died, and all Israel beat him, and they bury him in Arimathea, in his city; and Saul lifted out the ventriloquists, and the knowers from the land. And the foreigners gather, and come and encamp into Shunem. And Saul gathers every man of Israel, and they encamp into Gilboa. And Saul saw the foreigners’ camp, and feared, and his heart was astonished very much. And Saul asked through the Lord, and the Lord did not answer him in the dreams, and in the clear things, and in the prophets. And Saul said to his servants: Seek for me a ventriloquist woman, and I will go toward her, and seek in her. And his servants said toward him: Behold a ventriloquist woman in Endor. And the king said to her: Do not fear; say whom you have seen. And the woman said to him: I have seen gods going up from the earth. And he said to her: What have you known? title: Endor: demonic idol of Samuel; God may unveil woes even thus
english: earth, and worshiped him. And Samuel said: Why have you troubled me to lead me up? And Saul said: I am afflicted very much, and the foreigners are warring against me, and God has stood away from me, and has not still heard me, both in hand of the prophets, and in the dreams; and now I have called you to make known to me what I shall do. And Samuel said: Why do you ask me, and the Lord has stood away from you, and has come to be with your neighbor? and the Lord has done to you as the Lord spoke in my hand; and the Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand, and will give it to your neighbor David; because you did not hear the Lord’s voice, and did not fill his wrath’s anger in Amalek, on account of this the Lord has done the word to you on this day; and the Lord will hand over Israel with you into foreigners’ hands, and tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall, and the Lord will give Israel’s camp into foreigners’ hands.’ Is it then still lawful for you to hesitate, that Saul has melted away condemned by his own votes? For since he was fearing the weakness unto battle of those gathered against him, he was claiming to learn the things about to be from God. And when that one was silent, and unveiling nothing, he turns toward grieving the one who has chosen to be silent. And he arrives unto necromancy, although he had wiped out, it says, the knowers—I mean those thinking to know the things about to be. Then he says: ‘Lead up Samuel for me,’ not as if the charm or the magicians’ art were able to bring the holy one’s soul, but as those divinizing always using such a voice; and I have learned that with certain unspeakable words bewitching the demons, and charming water, they look down upon idols and shadows, and as in a mirror shapes of some, the demons perhaps fashionably molding the figures of those said to be brought up. And indeed the little woman said at the beginnings: I see gods going up from the earth. Then after this: ‘And the woman,’ it says, ‘saw Samuel.’ And nothing hard, that in equal and like shape of blessed Samuel a shadow and idol was seen, formed from demonic working. If then someone should think the prophet’s soul was truly called up, and will vote the true for the little woman’s words, since she says she has also seen gods going up from the earth, then let him also gift the lie to the customs of the divination, yet let him think according to truth that there are also some gods of such a rank who have risen from the earth—although God by nature is one and alone.

Palladius: You have spoken rightly. Yet someone, I think, will say: And yet he has spoken true things about to be when Saul was curious. And no small word has been spent by us proving that the truth is not in unclean spirits.

title: Foreknowledge as firstfruit of wrath; Balaam hired to curse
english: ls sounding according to likelihood into a human mind, which things if those who have chosen to be curious should learn, they will melt very much, and as it were some firstfruit of the wrath and justice hung over them they undergo the foreknowledge. For upon holy prophets he rests, and often shares, not only the gloomy things alone, and upon which someone having scowled would sit of tears, but also as many as will be for some unto good-cheer and fair-day; yet to unholy and most accursed love-diviners he thoroughly unveils the evils about to be for themselves.
Palladius: And what or from where would the assurance of these things be for us?

Cyril: From the sacred Letters; for a type and manner of mystagogy has been written for us—the things that befell the more ancient. Or do you not know that Balak the of Zippor, the tyrant of Moabites and Midianites, having dreaded Israel’s unconquerable and unbroken multitude, and having believed he would at once be destroyed together with the other nations, was hiring Balaam? ‘Come then,’ saying, ‘curse Israel for me.’ And when the ambassadors had come: ‘Lodge the night,’ he says, ‘and I will answer you a matter which the Lord should speak toward me.’ And seeking cold and demonic dreamlets, and expecting things happening for him perhaps from a charm and also sorcery, he said the Lord would speak to him; for he was pretending to call-upon-God. Yet even if the sacred Letter uses the customary voices of the sorcerers, we would not think, thinking rightly, that God who is by nature and truly sends the true as from love into profane souls, and talks toward a foul man and sorcerer and idolater. Yet, ‘God came,’ it says, ‘toward Balaam, and said to him: What are these humans beside you?’ And when that one had announced the cause of the arrival, ‘God said,’ it says, ‘toward Balaam: You will not go with them, nor will you curse the people; for it is blessed.’ Behold clearly from God’s person the blessed angel turns away the deceiver and empty-speaker sorcerer from seeking to curse the one blessed beside God, and from setting opposite the votes from above the inventions from human ill-counsel—not as if the curse were strong to wrong, but in order that the one who has unreasonably received such a hope might be clearly and evidently informed, and through him, that Israel would never become catchable for Moabites or Midianites, God shielding and contending, and walling with favors the people clinging to him and having been blessed. Yet these things the divine angel both said and was commanding to do; and when the diviner was baited by the promises of gifts unto needing to walk, having perhaps also truly supposed he would be strong, the blessed angel allows to go, yet was seen in the middle of the road, with a flashing sword, teaching clearly that the war for him is toward both God and angels, if he should wish to curse the blessed ones. And when he had arrived toward the Midianite, he was raising altars, and

title: Balaam blesses; God scatters false prophecy; stars cannot save
english: was ordering to sacrifice oxen; yet at once he was a prophet, not the customary and false-speaker, but by a divine and unspeakable power he was turned contrary to hope toward the opposite. For he was cursing not at all, yet was rather blessing Israel, and sends bitter griefs into Balak. And it has been written thus: that ‘Balak was wroth and clapped with his hands, and Balak said toward Balaam: I have called you to curse my enemy, and behold blessing you have blessed this third time. And Balaam said toward Balak: Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent toward me, saying: If Balak should give me his house full of silver and gold, I will not be able to pass by the Lord’s word to do it good or evil from myself? as many as God should say to me, these I will say.’ Customary then for the false-diviners also to use voices so deceptive, considering that altogether and in every way they will say the true to those wishing to be curious. Yet understand that saying the exact is foreign to the enchanter’s and magician’s art; and it would sometimes be added from God upon terribly putting to sleep the profane souls by the foretelling of the things about to be.
Palladius: I am persuaded.

Cyril: For that God has hated and loosens such—or rather sorceries and empty-speakings—would become clear when he says: ‘I am the Lord God;’ and besides these: ‘Who else will scatter signs of ventriloquists and the prophecies from a heart, turning wise ones backward, and making foolish their counsel, and standing words of his child and making true the counsel of his angels?’ For the prophecies from a heart he shows stale and false-speaking; yet of his own child—that is Christ—he stands every word; and the counsel of his angels—that is, as many as the heralds of the faith upon him should wish to speak—these he shows all full of truth, witnessing with signs and wonders, and the other workings of the Spirit. And he said somewhere again, reproaching some for the things adulterated by God’s law: ‘Stand then in your charms, and in your much pharmacy, which you were learning from your youth, if you will be able to be benefited; you have toiled in your counsels; let them stand and save you—the astrologers of the heaven, those seeing the stars; let them announce to you what is about to come upon you.’ You see then how God convicts the cursed star-sorcery as worthy of laughter and altogether useless. And that again the unerring would fit him and him alone, and the readiness unto words about the things expected to be without wandering, hear him saying through Isaiah’s voice: ‘Remember these things, and groan; repent, you who have wandered, turn in the heart, and remember the former things from the age; that I am God, and there is not besides me; announcing beforehand the last things before they come to be, and at once it was finished. And I said:

title: God alone foretells; fire-purification mocked; Greek myths
english: All my counsel will stand, and all as many as I wish, I will do.’ Alone then from our side will be laid down for the God beyond all, the being able both clearly to discern, and to foretell without wandering the things about to be; yet otherwise nonsense and old-wives’ little myths, buffooneries and trickings, the things from others, who having corrupted the mind speak the things from their own heart, according as it has been written, and make the lie a starting-point of money-talk.
Palladius: True. For it holds thus, and not otherwise.
Cyril: We will hold off then also from this, and having left a twisted path, we will walk the one unto the straight, clinging to God single-turned, and voting the truth for the saints’ voices.
Palladius: Very much.

Cyril: And why will we not also count that hated besides these, and say it is a portion of Greek godlessness—the loving somehow to be purified around by fire and water, and by some other such manners?
Palladius: And very much. Therefore also a divine oracle said clearly: ‘There will not be found in you one purifying his son or his daughter in fire.’

Cyril: How well the law was sounding these things to us, and refused the doing! For I think the matter is full of emptiness, and lacking the all-best and wise reasoning; for in what manner will fire’s nature benefit us? and torches running around in a circle how would they lift out the one who has sinned? For of bronze or then of some other such material, fire’s cast melts out the filth. Yet of mind and soul’s profanation, in what manner will it make disappear? Are these things then not already of laughter, and inventions of empty thoughts?
Palladius: Altogether so.

Cyril: And I would say as most sweetly to the select of Greeks, who have become inventors of such shameful practices, and introducers to the others: What then doing, O noble and wise ones, that Tityos whom you say was born from earth, you punish in Hades, setting vultures around him as diners of the livers, because having admired a little woman’s beauty he was sick with the desire? And for Tantalus you say a stone has been hung, and you mythologize to the young that he pays justices of an unbridled tongue? And having bound Ixion with long and always-moving turns of a wheel, you say he endures a penalty upon this, not out of tune with the gods from your deceit; yet yourselves and others although having fallen into terrible and most out-of-place evils, you free with fire and shoots, as you somehow think, and gift the washing-off of the charges, although very much condemned. And for Tityos, tell me, and those just now named, have you set a hard and inescapable justice—the perhaps coming to be in lack of fire? And indeed the most thieving according to you and carrier of fire to humans—I mean Prometheus, if somehow that one also was at all—was rich with fire’s use, and before
translator_notes: OET: no previous complete English of De adoratione Book 6 in PD; modern checks not copied as wording.

title: Prometheus aside; real stains vs fire/water; gnat and camel
english: the others; yet the myths beside you sing that he also has been wrapped in unbreakable bonds; and indeed they say hook-clawed vultures also flew upon him, as indeed also upon Tityos, terrible and wild punishers. Give then, give the cleansing through fire, not to those alone, but if also some of you should rage upon others’ daughters, or wives, doing what is not lawful, let these also having been freed from the charge by fire escape together with the stumblings the indictments; yet upon others at once courts and writings, and the evil-hating of the laws is shaken, yet yourselves practicing the all-shameful and foul-smelling life without discernment, you think to free from every pollution, having been deceived by cold and childish playthings, and taking as helpers unto this those most foul of the others; who also together with the figure, having let go the man-fitting word, are brought down toward women’s habits and manners both in bodies and judgments. Then in what manner will such a one purify? for being disposed thus, you will do some such thing, as if someone also seemed to perfume himself, yet having been smeared with some most unordered mire, then should think to set right and very well what had come unto his mind.
Palladius: You speak well; and I would agree with you speaking true things.

Cyril: And I pass by the folly in this at least, and will be silent for now about the servants of the cleansing, yet I go again unto the matter itself; and indeed I will also say that one would catch the worshipers of the demons living most mindlessly and most unlearnedly, neither understanding the manner of the wiping-out, nor indeed having exacted what ever pollution and profanation is according to truth; for adulteries and the still wilder passions than these, male-intercourses and murders, slanders and envies, false-prophecies and deceits, trickery and false-oath, would be stains and pollutions defiling soul and body, and having a hard-to-wash-out casting-out. Yet neither fire, nor springs of waters would wipe these things. And having left, I think somewhere, even only to know that they spot a soul, and make the mind full of foul smell, they stand off from dead bodies, and abominate the corrupted, dishonoring nature’s laws. And indeed also of foods which they should choose according to themselves they condemn understandingly, and if it should happen perhaps, even unwillingly to touch, at once leaping up they go upon the cleansing through fire or water, as if if they should only hold off from these, they will be holy and sincere. For they have been defeated thus of the glory, and have stood out of wits, upon which things one would also say very reasonably: ‘Woe to you, reinless and unlearned ones, straining out the gnat, yet gulping down the camel.’ For counting worthy of no word what knows how truly to defile, they have shuddered superfluously at the things upon which someone undergoes no harm.
